what_it_predicts: RMP depolarised; Rin lower at rest (open HCN is a conductance); sag larger at matched deflection and matched potential; rebound larger; ZD7288 or ivabradine hyperpolarise, reduce sag, and (as in the neocortical report cited by the paper) raise Rin; voltage-clamp Ih density or V1/2 differs

explanation: Recording or solution artefact: series or bridge resistance not balanced, selection by Rin and tau, differential cell health, uncorrected junction potential, bath K+ 3.5 mM
what_it_predicts: Apparent Rin and tau inflated in cells with higher access resistance (tolerated up to 40 Mohm against Rin 100-143 Mohm); a seal shunt would lower Rin and depolarise RMP (opposite for Rin); the junction offset is common to all genotypes so the contrast survives but absolute potentials and the comparison with E_K and HCN activation do not; selection by Rin and tau could create or hide a group difference
what_observed_fits_or_not: Cannot be excluded from the paper: access resistance by genotype and the bridge balance are not reported; the selection criteria include Rin and tau (O07); the junction offset cancels in the genotype contrast; a seal leak alone does not fit Rin up (but see A10: smaller cells plus a fixed seal leak); the HT and KO gene-dose gradient and the similar changes in three measures argue against a single random artefact but do not exclude a systematic difference in access

explanation: Network state of the KO slice: spontaneous bursting, synaptic bombardment, activity-dependent extracellular K+ rise in 36 of 42 KO slices
what_it_predicts: RMP depolarised through synaptic drive or raised [K+]o; Rin LOWER from synaptic shunting (INFERENZA for synaptic shunt; IPOTESI for raised [K+]o, which can act through Kir and rectification in either direction, not sourced here); rebound and sag altered by ongoing activity; the effect would be absent after synaptic blockade and partly present in HT slices that burst less
what_observed_fits_or_not: RMP fits; Rin higher does not fit shunting; HT shows RMP and Rin changes while bursting in 4 of 23 slices (O08, O12), which argues against a burst-driven effect as the whole story, but HT slices also differ from WT in mEPSC statistics (Fig 4 legend, pooled events) so a synaptic state without bursts is not excluded, and the Methods list no synaptic blocker (O07), so the recordings were probably unblocked; whether recordings were made under synaptic blockers is not stated

explanation: Transfer breaker: the Ih direction seen in GAERS thalamic neurons (more Ih with lower Rin, unchanged RMP and sag) is not the Wwox pattern

explanation: Smaller cells plus a fixed pipette-membrane seal leak (a constant shunt of unknown size)
what_it_predicts: Rin up (small cells have higher Rin), rest depolarised (a constant seal conductance depolarises a high-Rin small cell more than a large one), tau flat (tau = Rm x Cm does not depend on size), sag and rebound larger for a fixed -200 pA; seal quality would differ by cell and not by genotype unless cells are smaller
